title: Quantum steering is equivalent to state-preserving conditional expectations
authors: Lauritz van Luijk, Amine Marrakchi, Tobias Osborne, Alexander Stottmeister, Henrik Wilming
abstract: In systems with infinitely many degrees of freedom, fundamental results from quantum information theory can fail. An important example is the uniqueness of purifications: Even when two subsystems, described by commuting von Neumann algebras $A$ and $B$, are tomographically complete, purifications of a state on $A$ need not be related by unitaries in $B$. It was recently shown that this occurs precisely when Haag duality fails, i.e., when the commutant $B'$ is strictly larger than $A$. This raises the question of which fundamental entanglement properties survive in such a setting. We show that, for a pure global state, the ability to steer any ensemble decomposition of the marginal state on $A$ by measurements on $B$ is equivalent to the existence of a state-preserving conditional expectation from $B'$ onto $A$. This establishes a direct connection between quantum steering and subfactor theory. The key observation is that steering is equivalent to the existence of extensions of ensemble decompositions from $A$ to $B'$. Working with general Jordan algebras, we prove that unital positive maps have state-preserving left inverses if and only if ensemble decompositions can be lifted. For the inclusion $A\hookrightarrow B'$, a left inverse is precisely a conditional expectation, yielding the characterization above.
summary: This theoretical paper establishes a profound connection between the physical notion of quantum steering and abstract mathematics via conditional expectations. It proves that steering is equivalent to the existence of a state-preserving map from one subsystem's algebra ($B'$) onto another ($A$). This result provides powerful tools for analyzing entanglement in complex systems where standard assumptions about local structure break down.
main_problem: The paper investigates which fundamental entanglement properties survive in quantum systems with infinitely many degrees of freedom where Haag duality fails. It aims to connect the operational concept of 'quantum steering' to abstract algebraic structures.
main_result: For a pure global state, quantum steering is mathematically equivalent to the existence of a state-preserving conditional expectation from the commutant $B'$ onto the algebra $A$.
method: The proof involves establishing equivalences using ensemble decomposition properties and extending these arguments from general Jordan algebras to von Neumann algebras.
model_or_system: The analysis uses commuting von Neumann algebras $A$ and $B'$, modeling systems where Haag duality fails, such as those found in topologically ordered systems or 1+1-dimensional conformal field theories.
key_observables: Quantum steering capability (operational), existence of a state-preserving conditional expectation ($E: B' 	o A$), and the index of the subfactor inclusion $[B':A]$.
important_parameters:
The nature of the global state ($\omega$) is crucial, often restricted to pure states. The failure of Haag duality ($B'

main_assumptions: The analysis frequently restricts itself to pure global states and relies on advanced mathematical machinery from subfactor theory and operator algebras.

paper_structure: The paper develops the equivalence by first defining steering operationally, then linking it to an 'ensemble extension property,' and finally proving this link is equivalent to the existence of the required state-preserving conditional expectation $E: B' 	o A$.
why_interesting: It provides a deep mathematical characterization (via subfactor theory) for a physically intuitive concept (quantum steering), which has implications for understanding entanglement in complex, infinite quantum systems.

figures.caption: Figure 1: Examples; Bulk: A two-dimensional topologically ordered system is divided into a region A consisting of two disjoint infinite cones and their complement B. Boundary: A completely rational 1+1- dimensional conformal field theory is divided into a region A consisting of two disjoint intervals and their complement B. Haag duality fails in both settings and a normal conditional expectation B′ →A exists, so by Theorem B the relevant question is which state is preserved. For the surface code it is the ground state; for a completely rational chiral conformal net it cannot be the vacuum, because of the Reeh–Schlieder property.

Figure 2: The figure provides an overview of the logical dependencies and the proof structure of the results stated in the introduction. The left-hand column is the general theory of Section 2, which is carried out for normal unital positive maps between JBW*-algebras. the right-hand column provides the basic observations on steering. Theorem B combines the two: Lemma A turns steering into the ensemble extension property, Proposition E turns the latter into a state-preserving conditional expectation. Both items of Theorem C come out of Theorem B via the reduction of mixed states to pure ones.
